highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 introduces custom vertex meshes with SkSL programs for GPU-backed drawing.
highlights_body: This unreleased line also fixes Apple device framework packaging and brings Skia m159 fixes for glyph rendering, image-filter caching, and Imagination Vulkan allocation failures.

bullets.detail: Define SkSL vertex and fragment programs with SKMeshSpecification and its builder, then construct meshes with SKMeshBuilder or SKIndexedMeshBuilder and draw with SKCanvas.DrawMesh. Specifications support attributes, varyings, uniforms, and child effects; indexed meshes use 16-bit indices. Mesh drawing requires a GPU-backed surface and is a no-op on raster canvases.

SKMeshVertexBuffer and SKMeshIndexBuffer provide Create, Copy, and Update operations for CPU-backed buffers and GRContext-based Ganesh GPU buffers. Updates require 4-byte size and offset alignment. Built meshes retain native resources after specification, builder, buffer, and child-shader wrappers are disposed; disposing a builder leaves its shared specification intact.

SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp iOS and tvOS device frameworks now use arm64 device binaries and device platform metadata, correcting simulator slices and metadata that could cause App Store rejection ITMS-90087. Separate simulator frameworks continue to include x86_64 and arm64 slices.

Mask-filtered glyph rendering uses reloaded glyph state when a scaler changes paths, mask formats, or bounds, clears incompatible masks, and correctly copies clipped emboss masks. Image-filter cache key equality now matches bytewise hashing, including signed zero, cached matrix type masks, and subnormal translations.

Ganesh and Graphite abandon descriptor pools when allocation reports host or device out-of-memory on Imagination drivers, avoiding a driver failure when destroying the affected pool. Graphite also blocks further allocation through the abandoned handle. Other vendors and allocation errors are unaffected by this workaround.

contributor_summaries.kdpkke: Fixed iOS and tvOS device framework packaging for SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp while retaining both simulator architectures.
